---
title: "Logbook submissions the source merge left out"
author: "Einar Hjörleifsson"
date: today
---

```{r setup}
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(nanoparquet)
# quarto sets the working directory to this file's own; R/paths.R is the
# single place that resolves $FISHYDATA, and nothing here hardcodes a data path.
source("../R/paths.R")
loss <- read_parquet(fd_curated("check", "afli_rafr_stofn_loss.parquet"))
big  <- loss |> filter(stations_electronic >= 50)
```

*Measured with AI assistance (Claude); the decision is the maintainer's (decision 098, 2026-10-14).*

## The short version

`r format(sum(loss$stations_lost), big.mark = ",")` electronic afli logbook submissions from 2003–2019 never
reached the source system's merged table, so they are not in this logbook. **From September 2007 on, per-vessel
figures need no correction for them.** The landings show that the trips they belong to are complete without
them. Most are the same hauls submitted a second time.

Before September 2007 (1,854 of the rows, mostly 2004–2006) no landing can be linked, so nothing here can say
whether those are copies too.

## What the landings show

Each absent haul was placed on its trip with the same key the logbook uses (vessel, landing date, landing
harbour). The table compares each trip's logbook catch with its landing (2007-09 to 2019, trips with one landing).

| trips | n | logbook / landed |
|---|---|---|
| no absent haul (for comparison) | 560,513 | 0.984 |
| absent hauls with catch: logbook as it is | 3,142 | 0.987 |
| the same trips with the absent hauls added | 3,142 | 1.772 |

- Without the absent hauls, these trips match their landings as well as any trip does.
- With them, 60 % of the trips go more than 30 % over the landing.
- 1,288 trips are absent whole. For most of them the vessel's landing within two days is already linked to a
  logbook trip that is present.

## What they are

- A third of the absent hauls with catch (31–68 % in 2011–2017) have an exact copy among the hauls that are
  present: same vessel, same catch of every species, mostly the same day and position.
- The copy is in another submission, so a check within one submission does not find it.
- In 2004–2010 there are few exact copies, but the landings still show those trips complete.
- Their positions lie on the vessel's AIS track nearly as often as those of the hauls that are present (91 %
  against 97 % within 5 km). A copy of a real haul would do the same.

## Still open

- **About 410 trips absent whole that do have a landing no logbook trip took.** They are the only candidates for
  genuinely missing records, and nothing here proves them.
- **The rows before September 2007**, which no landing link reaches.

## Share absent by year

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 3
#| fig-width: 8
tibble(
  year = c(2003:2020),
  pct  = c(3.49, 19.14, 5.27, 5.14, 5.00, 6.28, 2.21, 2.81, 3.26, 2.35,
           2.20, 2.35, 1.53, 1.36, 1.52, 0.58, 0.02, 0.02)) |>
  ggplot(aes(year, pct)) +
  geom_line(colour = "grey30") + geom_point(colour = "grey30") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2004, 2020, 4)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "% of that year's submissions absent") +
  theme_minimal()
```

The share is highest at the start of electronic reporting (19 % in 2004) and falls to 0.02 % by 2019.

## Vessels with the largest share absent

This is where the feed and the merge differ most. From 2007-09 it is not a measure of error in a vessel's figures.

```{r}
#| echo: false
big |>
  slice_max(pct_lost, n = 15) |>
  transmute(vid, vessel, `call sign` = coalesce(cs, "—"),
            `submissions` = stations_electronic, `absent` = stations_lost,
            `% absent` = round(pct_lost, 1), `years` = paste0(first_year, "–", last_year)) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

## Provenance

`curate/checks/afli_rafr_stofn_loss.R` writes `curated/check/afli_rafr_stofn_loss.parquet`, one row per vessel.
The defect and its close are in `curate/corrections/afli_rafr_stofn_stations_dropped.yml` and
`curate/decisions/098-dropped-afli-hauls-not-admitted.md`. The measurement scripts are in
`$FISHYDATA/archive/2026-10-todo19/`.
